title: Files and Folder Structure
summary: A tour of what the CLI creates and which files matter most.
heading: Files and Folder Structure

blocks.text: It looks like a lot of files at first, but you'll only touch a few of them day to day. Here's the shape of a fresh app.

blocks.label: my-app/
blocks.code:
my-app/
├─ src/
│  ├─ app/
│  │  ├─ app.ts          # root component (a class)
│  │  ├─ app.html        # its template
│  │  ├─ app.css         # its styles
│  │  ├─ app.config.ts   # app-wide setup
│  │  └─ app.routes.ts   # page routes
│  ├─ main.ts            # starts the app
│  ├─ index.html         # the single HTML page
│  └─ styles.css         # global styles
├─ public/               # images & static files
├─ angular.json          # build settings
├─ package.json          # dependencies & scripts
└─ tsconfig.json         # TypeScript settings

blocks.text: Depending on the Angular version, the root files may be named app.ts or app.component.ts. The idea is the same either way.

layers.title: src/app/
layers.detail: Your components live here — this is where you spend most of your time

layers.title: main.ts
layers.detail: The starting point that boots the app (you rarely change it)

layers.title: index.html
layers.detail: The one real HTML page; your whole app loads inside it

layers.title: styles.css
layers.detail: Global styles for the entire app

layers.title: app.config.ts
layers.detail: App-wide setup, like the router and HttpClient

layers.title: package.json
layers.detail: Lists your dependencies and the npm scripts (like start and build)

blocks.text: A component is usually a small group of files with the same name: the class, its template, and its styles. The class ties them together with a @Component label on top.

blocks.label: hello.ts

blocks.text: Look closely: it's just a class (Chapter 8) with a label, it imports from a module (Chapter 9), and the template shows data with {{ }} (Chapter 6). You already know the pieces.

items: Most of your work happens in src/app/.
styles.css is global; component styles stay with the component.
A component is a class + template + styles, joined by @Component.
